seoTitle: Use TradingView Paper Trading & Fix a Missing Panel
metaDescription: Enable TradingView Paper Trading, place market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders, attach stop loss and take profit, and fix the panel when it won't show.
intro:
Practicing trades without risking real money is what TradingView's Paper Trading is built for, but plenty of users hit the same two snags: the panel won't show up, or they're not sure how bracket orders behave once submitted.

This guide walks through the real Paper Trading panel: account settings, the order ticket, and the positions view, so you can place trades, attach exits, and read your results the way you would on a live account. It ends with the fix for the panel-not-visible problem, which is a layout issue almost every time, not an account one.
costNote: Paper Trading itself is free on every TradingView plan, including the Basic (free) tier, with a starting virtual balance you set yourself. That's separate from Bar Replay, which now requires at least the Essential plan; the two features are often confused because they sit near each other on the chart.

steps.heading: Switch to the Paper Trading tab
steps.body: On any TradingView chart, the trading panel at the bottom lists the brokers you can connect, with Paper Trading, powered by TradingView, at the top. Selecting it opens a simulated account that fills against live or near-live prices using virtual funds. If the tab isn't there at all, the bottom panel is almost certainly collapsed, not the feature being unavailable; the fix is at the end of this guide.

steps.heading: Set up or reset your paper account
steps.body: Before your first trade, open Account settings to configure the account. You can reset it entirely, wiping orders, history, and positions and resetting the balance to a value you choose, and set separate leverage ratios per asset class (stocks, futures, forex, crypto). This matters because a fresh account's default leverage may not match what a live broker gives you: testing a strategy at 50:1 forex leverage when your real broker offers 10:1 teaches the wrong lessons.

image.caption: The Reset account dialog, where you set a starting balance and per-asset leverage before wiping an existing paper account clean.

steps.heading: Place an order
steps.body: Click a symbol on your watchlist to load it, then use Buy or Sell at the top of the order ticket. TradingView supports four order types here: Market (fills immediately at the best available price), Limit (fills only at your price or better), Stop (turns into a market order once a trigger price is hit), and Stop-Limit (a trigger price that then submits a limit order instead of a market one). Which one fits depends on whether you want the fill guaranteed or the price guaranteed; you can't have both.

steps.heading: Attach a stop loss and take profit
steps.body: The order ticket's Exits section lets you turn on a take-profit price and a stop-loss price, either as an exact price or in ticks from your entry. TradingView validates these as you type; a stop loss on a long position has to sit below your entry, and it will flag a price that doesn't. Set both and you have a bracket order: once either the stop or the target fills, TradingView automatically cancels the other, so you're never left with a stray exit order after the position closes. The order info panel shows margin usage and leverage in real time as you set the size.

image.caption: The order ticket with Take profit and Stop loss fields filled in below the Buy/Sell buttons, plus a live margin and leverage readout.

steps.heading: Track positions, orders, and results
steps.body: Once a trade fills, the bottom panel switches to Positions, with running Account Balance, Equity, Realized P&L, and Unrealized P&L updating as price moves. Orders and Order History log every fill and pending order, and Trading Journal keeps a timestamped record of activations and executions, useful for reviewing a session afterward instead of relying on memory.

image.caption: The Paper Trading panel after a trade fills, showing account balance, equity, open orders, and a timestamped trading journal entry.

steps.heading: Fix the panel when it's not visible
steps.body:
TradingView's own documentation for collapsed panes gives two ways back in. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Cmd (Mac) and double-click anywhere inside the collapsed bottom pane to restore it. If a Collapse Pane button is visible in the pane's corner, clicking it toggles the same thing (turn its visibility on under Chart Settings > Canvas if you don't see it).

If that doesn't bring the tab back, check that a different broker isn't already selected in the panel instead of Paper Trading. As a last resort, reset the chart layout to TradingView's default: this only affects which panels and toolbars show, not your paper account, balance, or trade history, and it clears most layout conflicts a saved session can carry over.

troubleshooting.problem: The Paper Trading tab is missing from the bottom of the chart
troubleshooting.cause: The bottom pane is collapsed, which can happen from an accidental drag or shortcut.
troubleshooting.fix: Hold Ctrl/Cmd and double-click inside the collapsed pane, or use the Collapse Pane button in its corner if it's enabled in Chart Settings > Canvas.

troubleshooting.problem: The panel is visible but shows a different broker, not Paper Trading
troubleshooting.cause: Another connected broker is currently selected in the trading panel's broker list.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the broker dropdown at the top of the panel and select Paper Trading, powered by TradingView.

troubleshooting.problem: Nothing above works and the layout still looks wrong
troubleshooting.cause: A saved custom layout is carrying panel-visibility settings from a previous session.
troubleshooting.fix: Reset the chart layout to TradingView's default. It doesn't touch your paper account balance or trade history, only which panels are shown.

troubleshooting.problem: A stop-loss or take-profit price gets rejected when submitting
troubleshooting.cause: The price is on the wrong side of your entry, for example a stop above entry on a long position.
troubleshooting.fix: Adjust the price so the stop sits below entry (long) or above entry (short), which is what TradingView's validation is checking for.

faq.question: Is Paper Trading free on TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, on every plan including the free Basic tier. You choose your own starting balance when you set up or reset the account.

faq.question: Does Paper Trading use real market prices?
faq.answer: Yes. It fills against live or near-real-time market prices while simulating the trade with virtual funds instead of real money.

faq.question: What order types can I use in Paper Trading?
faq.answer: Market, Limit, Stop, and Stop-Limit. Market and Stop guarantee a fill; Limit and Stop-Limit guarantee a price, at the risk of not filling at all if the market moves past it.

faq.question: What happens when I set both a stop loss and a take profit?
faq.answer: That's a bracket order. When either one fills, TradingView automatically cancels the other, so a closed position doesn't leave a stray exit order behind.

faq.question: Why is my Paper Trading panel not showing up?
faq.answer: Almost always a collapsed bottom pane. Hold Ctrl/Cmd and double-click inside it to restore, or reset the chart layout to default if that doesn't work.

faq.question: Can I reset my paper trading balance?
faq.answer: Yes, from Account settings. Resetting clears orders, history, and positions and lets you set a new starting balance and leverage for each asset class.
